translations.text: There was one called David, a humble-minded hero, ruler of the Israelites, noble and powerful, the choicest of kings, dearest to Christ.
Under the heavens he was the most famous of harpers that we have heard of among the peoples.
He was a most truthful singer, and he took great care to intercede for his people with the most merciful Creator of men.
David, the Lord's servant, was a true and victorious champion in war, a skilful man, a cunning emperor, whenever the clash of battle-banners had to come about in days of strife.
Yet it befell him, as very often happens, that the good-hearted commit sin through the passing thoughts of the body.

It came about that the Saviour of souls, the Lord of hosts, sent to him a prophet with words, and commanded him to tell him, to make known to him personally, the Ruler's judgment on his evil deeds: that the prince had forfeited his life,

because he had ordered Uriah to be deprived of life, had suddenly robbed a brave warrior of his life, and had taken Bathsheba as his wife out of greed, for which he soon felt God's anger through his own deed.

Then the prince of the people, David, earnestly pleaded and prayed to the Lord. He himself unlocked his hoard of sins, earnestly confessed his guilt to God, the Lord of hosts, and spoke thus in words:
"Have mercy on me, Ruler of powers, since you know the thoughts of men. Help, my Saviour, almighty God, the work of your own hands alone, according to your great mercy.
"And also, according to the multitude of your mercies, Lord of hosts, blot out my iniquity, as forgiveness for my spirit,
Wash me from sins, and my soul from stains, Creator of spirits. Cleanse the offences that I have ever committed in my life through the wicked thoughts of the body.

For I acknowledge all my wrongdoing, and every one of my sins is before my own eyes. The throng of my wicked deeds stands before me, and my guilt shines out. Forgive me, my Creator, source of the light of life, and grant me the joy of your love.
I have often sinned against you alone, and I have also done many evils, hostile-minded in my offences. I ask you for help, Lord of spirits, saving Christ,
so that, with my spirit's wounds forgiven, I may journey on into the world to come, so that your sayings may be fulfilled, that you do not desire the death of any man.
for you have always taught sinners to turn and obey Christ, and so gain long life with you, just as you, Lord, Saviour of souls, overcame every kind of sin at the judgement.
I was conceived in iniquities and also in sins. You alone know, mighty Lord, how my mother bore me in shame and in guilt.
Grant me, my Creator, that I myself may turn away from the sins that my forefathers committed before me and that I myself also practised afterwards.

But you, God yourself, love truth alone. Therefore I will pray to you with petitions for life and grace, prince of light, because you yourself have unlocked for me the unknown and hidden hoard of your wisdom.
Mighty God, gentle and kind, purify me wholly with hyssop. Then, cleansed, I will praise Christ, and, myself shining beyond snow, I will soon find the love of your peace.
Open now, almighty one, the hearing of my ears, so that my hearing may become joyful in gladness, turned forward toward you.
Then, Ruler, gentle Lord, the broken bones that were for a while in humiliation will be in joy for ever.
Turn your face away now from my sins and from the misdeeds of my offences, Saviour of souls, almighty God, and through the mercy of your powers blot out all my wrongdoing.
Increase [?] a clean heart in me, Lord Christ, mighty God, and a steadfast mind to accept your will and to keep holy laws. And, Ruler of the heavens, firmly renew a right spirit within me.
Do not cast me away, Lord of hosts, from the sight of all your mercies, and do not take the good Holy Spirit from me, Lord, almighty lord. Do not wholly deprive me of your favours.

Give me now joy, gentle Lord, the hope of your salvation, protector of all creatures. And strengthen me with your spirit, living shepherd of light, God himself, so that from now on I may always wholly conform to your will.

I have always taught your ways to the heedless, so that the impious might turn back to the shepherd of their own souls, to God himself, and seek protection for their spirits from you through the love of peace.

Free me in spirit, Father of mankind, from bloodshed and wicked hostilities, living God. Cleanse my offences, Saviour and helper, guardian of the kingdom of heaven. Then my tongue will rejoice faithfully in your own righteousness.
Open now, ruling God, my lips, so that my mouth may afterwards eagerly declare your powers and your praise to the joy of the people, true Lord of victory.
I would have brought you sacrifice at once, Lord of hosts, had you wished it so; but you did not love it, ruler of life, that I should bring you burnt offerings of dead cattle as the Lord's will.
But much more pleasing to you, mighty Lord, living Christ, is the broken spirit, the heart cleansed and humbled in its thoughts. These you, almighty one, never despise.

Now, living God, grant your helpful comfort according to the will of your good spirit, so that Mount Zion may be victorious and the walls of Zion, of Jerusalem, may be strengthened and made secure in joy.
So you, mighty lord, Saviour of men, will afterwards accept the loving offering of your peoples. They will willingly set the holy calf on your altar, prince of light."

Grant me, living Creator of mankind, mighty Lord, that the sorrowful wounds of my soul, the reckless sins I have committed in the flesh in old age or in youth, may be forgiven by your spirit through your love and slip away."
So the prince of the people, David, pleaded with the Lord, mindful of his deeds, that mighty God, Christ the Saviour, the ruling God, would protect him as worthy of the kingdom, as a comfort to men.
So he made amends with humble thought for the hoard of evil deeds he had committed in his heart, the wounds of the spirit.
Grant us, mighty God, that we may always overcome the hoard of sins and earn for ourselves eternal joys in the delight of the land of the living. Amen.
